source: based on the 27 curated Lean source declarations in proofs-01/02/03.json; explanations are interpretive and do not broaden their exact scopes

entries.plain: Splitting a fixed mass into two positive portions always raises the sum of the minimum energies, within the proved parameter range.
entries.why: This strict energy gap is the binding step used when ruling out fragmentation of a minimizing sequence.
entries.conditions: In the two-dimensional cubic–quintic setting: β, γ > 0; 0 < m ≤ mB; and every 0 < μ < m.

entries.plain: Starting sufficiently close to the set of energy minimizers keeps the solution close to that entire set for all time.
entries.why: The theorem turns variational information into a dynamical stability statement, without choosing a unique wave profile.
entries.conditions: The specified 2D equation, β, γ > 0, 0 < m ≤ mB, with distance measured in H².

entries.plain: Every allowed H² initial state has exactly one solution defined for all positive and negative times.
entries.why: Global existence and uniqueness supply the evolution needed by the subsequent stability theorem.
entries.conditions: The specific two-dimensional fourth-order cubic–quintic evolution with γ > 0 and initial data in H².
entries.math: \forall u_0\in H^2(\mathbb R^2),\quad \exists!\,u:\mathbb R\to H^2(\mathbb R^2)

entries.plain: The lowest constrained energy is achieved by at least one actual H² field, not merely approached by a sequence.
entries.why: Attainment establishes a nonempty minimizing set on which the later orbital-stability statement is formulated.
entries.conditions: Two-dimensional model; β, γ > 0; 0 < m ≤ mB. The result does not select a unique profile.

entries.plain: For a weighted phase problem with winding, the minimum energy and the phases achieving it are characterized exactly.
entries.why: The result separates an unavoidable global mismatch cost from a nonnegative deviation term.
entries.conditions: The declared positive-weight, integrability and H¹ phase assumptions in PhaseLockingData.

entries.plain: At any allowed state, a nearby field with the same mass can be found that has lower curvature energy.
entries.why: This local descent direction rules out positive-curvature constrained local minimizers in the specified model.
entries.conditions: Dimensions 1–4; positive leading coefficient; nonnegative second coefficient; regularization assumptions.

entries.plain: A particular quantified gradient estimate works precisely in dimension two.
entries.why: It identifies a sharp dimensional boundary for this one functional estimate, not for localization in general.
entries.conditions: Spatial dimension n ≥ 1; the exact E68L2Holds predicate defined in the source.

entries.plain: A nonzero square-integrable field cannot put all its Fourier content on an infinitely thin frequency sphere.
entries.why: A sphere has zero ambient measure, so L² spectral localization requires more than exact shell support.
entries.conditions: Whole-space L² functions and the specified almost-everywhere Fourier-support hypothesis.

entries.plain: The defined Fourier-multiplier evolution never increases the L² norm.
entries.why: A contraction estimate is a precise stability property of a linear propagation operator.
entries.conditions: The specified multiplier semigroup, with a ≥ 0 and time t ≥ 0.

entries.plain: Nearby, genuinely different parameter choices can give the same eleven observations.
entries.why: The local twenty-dimensional fiber shows structural ambiguity, beyond numerical ill-conditioning.
entries.conditions: The frozen 31-parameter / 11-observation nonlinear map, with α ≥ 0.

entries.plain: At the chosen model point, the observation Jacobian has twenty undetectable local parameter directions.
entries.why: The nullity calculation supplies the differential rank condition behind local non-identifiability.
entries.conditions: The specified frozen observation map; α ≥ 0. This is a local Jacobian result.

entries.plain: The listed symmetry and regularization requirements admit infinitely many distinct curvature closures.
entries.why: Those conditions alone cannot uniquely determine the closure, so additional mathematical axioms would be needed.
entries.conditions: The specified smooth regularized closure family with ε > 0 and S > 0.

entries.plain: Two different closure formulas can be distinguished by evaluating them on a genuine smooth field.
entries.why: This rules out interpreting closure nonuniqueness as a merely formal difference between expressions.
entries.conditions: Two distinct closure parameters, ε > 0 and S > 0, in the declared smooth-field family.

entries.plain: In the specified auxiliary-variable Hamiltonian, changing one momentum makes the energy arbitrarily negative.
entries.why: Introducing auxiliary variables does not remove this particular unbounded direction.
entries.conditions: The reduced temporal-jet Hamiltonian with the indicated configuration coordinate Q ≠ 0.

entries.plain: An invertible change of the chosen field variables cannot make the nonzero acceleration Hessian degenerate.
entries.why: The determinant keeps a positive square factor under the allowed coordinate transformation.
entries.conditions: Nonzero Hessian coefficient and nonzero Jacobian determinant of the point transformation.

entries.plain: A zero-frequency onset at positive wave number forces an instability already in the zero-wave-number sector.
entries.why: This excludes a primary finite-wave-number static onset within that parameter sector.
entries.conditions: The stated homogeneous S004 inverse propagator, K > 0, positive curvature gap, and q > 0.

entries.plain: Under the specified positive-stiffness assumptions, a static zero at positive wave number cannot occur.
entries.why: The inverse propagator has a strict sign, so it cannot vanish under those hypotheses.
entries.conditions: K > 0, 4KT − G² > 0, nonnegative mass-squared, and q > 0.

entries.plain: The corrected complex-field regularizer stays strictly positive, preventing this denominator from vanishing.
entries.why: This establishes a well-defined local expression at the algebraic level, including zero-field nodes.
entries.conditions: Complex field value arbitrary, regularization ε > 0, and the specified denominator.

entries.plain: Under exchangeability, the exact finite-sample randomization p-value obeys the advertised type-I error bound.
entries.why: It validates the statistical testing rule under its null assumptions, not any measured optical effect.
entries.conditions: A finite exchangeable null model and a nonnegative significance level.

entries.plain: The defined phase-correction coefficient satisfies the exact integer-winding closure identity.
entries.why: The arithmetic ensures consistency of the scalar phase-lock construction.
entries.conditions: An integer winding and a nonzero integrated reciprocal-weight denominator.

entries.plain: A real scalar mode satisfying the stipulated cubic-saturation ODE obeys a precise power-growth inequality.
entries.why: This captures one reduced amplitude law without assuming the same estimate for a full nonlinear PDE.
entries.conditions: A differentiable real amplitude with the displayed scalar evolution at the evaluated time.

entries.plain: Two different internal block states can produce the same defined readout.
entries.why: The output map is non-injective; this is a structural information-loss fact, not a cryptographic security guarantee.
entries.conditions: The finite-state squeezeRound construction defined in the public WaveLock source.

entries.plain: The constructed L² Fourier transform preserves the norm of a field.
entries.why: Unitarity is a foundation for the surrounding whole-space Fourier analysis.
entries.conditions: The formal L² space and Fourier extension in this module.

entries.plain: A particular dispersion branch has its unique minimum at a strictly positive wave number.
entries.why: It establishes linear spectral preference at a finite scale, but not nonlinear selection of a stable pattern.
entries.conditions: The module's Base and FiniteScale hypotheses for the real dispersion branch.

entries.plain: For the specified nonlinear dynamics, a state built from two nonzero Fourier modes immediately generates a mode outside the chosen finite set.
entries.why: The resulting frequency leakage obstructs exact invariance of such finite-dimensional mode spaces.
entries.conditions: At least two allowed wave vectors, a nonzero quintic coupling, and two nonzero coefficients.

entries.plain: Smooth periodic solutions can start arbitrarily small in one jet norm yet reach a fixed size later.
entries.why: That behavior rules out a bounded evolution map between the stated initial and later jet spaces.
entries.conditions: The specific torus higher-time-derivative equation, positive time and allowed Sobolev jet exponents.

entries.plain: A complex scalar's real-gradient Gram tensor has rank at most two on a four-dimensional tangent space.
entries.why: This particular construction cannot define a nondegenerate Lorentzian metric, without ruling out other metric constructions.
entries.conditions: A C¹ complex scalar on the specified four-dimensional smooth manifold.
